title: Streaming micro-batch layer with hot-key mitigation for console metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Console telemetry is dominated by a long tail of tiny events (single-metric pings, route-heartbeats, and ephemeral UI traces). These tiny records cause high per-message CPU overhead, high broker pressure, and elevated 99th-percentile ingest latency during traffic spikes. Goal: introduce a streaming micro-batch layer that groups short-lived console metric events into per-tenant micro-batches to amortize overhead while preserving low tail latency and deterministic ordering where required. Key constraints: multi-tenant isolation, hot-key (single-route/tenant) spikes, compatibility with current exactly-once downstream merging, and minimal schema changes for downstream consumers.

Design summary: implement a shard-local micro-batcher that operates between the ingress gateway and existing stream processors. The layer uses adaptive, workload-aware windows: default target window 25ms with bounds [5ms, 250ms] and a dynamic adjuster driven by queue depth and measured downstream lag. Micro-batches are namespace-scoped (tenant + route) but coalesced into physical batch bundles to avoid creating many tiny partitions. Hot-key mitigation: we detect hot keys using a lightweight local Count-Min sketch and, upon detection, route hot-key traffic to dedicated hot partitions with separate batching policies (smaller windows, larger throughput streams) and an LRU hot-key map to avoid unbounded state. Ordering semantics: ordering is preserved within a micro-batch and we attach deterministic per-event sequence numbers so downstream merge logic can reconstruct strict ordering where needed. Delivery semantics: keep at-least-once to minimize complexity, but add an idempotent batch-level merge key (batch_id + seq-range) so downstream consumers can dedupe efficiently. Backpressure & flow control: credit-based tokens propagated from downstream to control micro-batch flush if consumers are slow; when tokens are exhausted, we favor latency by progressively reducing batch windows (trade-off to avoid head-of-line blocking).

Trade-offs considered: 1) Exactly-once would require transactional writes and cross-shard coordination—decided to postpone due to complexity and performance cost. 2) Per-tenant batch isolation improves billing accuracy but increases number of in-flight batches—we balance by coalescing at physical layer. 3) Hot-key dedicated partitions improve latency for heavy routes but complicate capacity planning; mitigation will be automated by autoscaler heuristics.

Telemetry & SLOs: ingest 99th percentile latency target <= 120ms for normal traffic; tail during 5x traffic spikes <= 500ms. CPU cost per-million-events should drop by ~12% in synthetic load tests.

Acceptance criteria: 1) End-to-end benchmark demonstrating >=10% CPU reduction and 99p ingest latency <= 120ms on baseline workload. 2) Integration tests for ordering and dedup with existing downstream merge consumer. 3) Feature gated behind a rollout flag per-cluster and per-tenant. 4) Dashboard with per-tenant micro-batch size, hot-key detection rate, and backpressure signals.

Rollout plan: start in canary on internal telemetry cluster (canary-1) for 2 weeks, synthetic spike tests, then progressive enablement for low-traffic tenants, followed by automated ramp for higher tiers with fallback toggle and capacity autoscaler policy tuned for hot partitions.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark shows >=10% CPU reduction on representative workload
Ordering/dedup integration tests pass with downstream merge consumer
Feature flag and per-tenant rollout controls implemented
Dashboards for micro-batch metrics and hot-key alerts live in console
comments: 2025-12-03 - Triage: identified as high ROI for cost and latency. Assigned to Liam for design spike.
2025-12-15 - Design review: raised concerns about unbounded hot-key map. Agreed to LRU eviction and eviction metrics.
2026-01-08 - Implementation: initial micro-batcher prototype added to ingest service; basic adaptive window logic working locally.
2026-01-21 - Perf run: synthetic load shows 9% CPU improvement; 99p latency improved ~85ms -> 105ms. Need further tuning for hot-key heavy patterns.
2026-02-05 - Review feedback from Platform: add credit-based backpressure and an explicit fallback to immediate flush for high-priority events.
